16	package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.service;
17	
18	import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
19	
20	/**
21	 * Formats an owner's {@code customerCode} as {@code '<LAST3>-<NNNN>'}, where {@code LAST3}
22	 * is the upper-cased first three letters of the last name and {@code NNNN} is a zero-padded
23	 * 4-digit sequence number (e.g. {@code 'SMI-0007'}).
24	 */
25	@Component
26	public class CustomerCodeGenerator {
27	
28	    /**
29	     * Build the customer code for the given last name and global sequence number.
30	     *
31	     * @param lastName the owner's last name (its first three letters, upper-cased, form the prefix)
32	     * @param sequence the 4-digit global sequence number
33	     * @return the formatted customer code
34	     */
35	    public String generate(String lastName, long sequence) {
36	        String prefix = lastName.substring(0, Math.min(3, lastName.length())).toUpperCase();
37	        return String.format("%s-%04d", prefix, sequence);
38	    }
39	}

20	import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model.Owner;
21	import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
22	
23	/**
24	 * Counts how many existing owners share a candidate owner's first and last name,
25	 * comparing both names case-insensitively.
26	 */
27	@Component
28	public class NamesakeCounter {
29	
30	    /**
31	     * Count the owners in {@code existingOwners} whose first and last name match the
32	     * candidate's, ignoring case.
33	     *
34	     * @param candidate      the owner being created
35	     * @param existingOwners the owners to compare against (the candidate itself must not be included)
36	     * @return the number of matching namesakes
37	     */
38	    public int count(Owner candidate, Collection<Owner> existingOwners) {
39	        String firstName = candidate.getFirstName();
40	        String lastName = candidate.getLastName();
41	        return (int) existingOwners.stream()
42	            .filter(existing -> firstName.equalsIgnoreCase(existing.getFirstName())
43	                && lastName.equalsIgnoreCase(existing.getLastName()))
44	            .count();
45	    }
46	}

## Summary

I changed the `customerCode` format from `<LAST3>-<NNNN>` to `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>` with a per-city sequence, keeping each responsibility in its natural place:

**`CustomerCodeGenerator`** (formatting) — `generate` now takes `city, lastName, sequence` and produces `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>` (e.g. `LON-SMI-0007`). Since the city and last-name prefixes share the same "first three, upper-cased" rule, I extracted a private `prefix(...)` helper so the logic isn't duplicated.

**`ClinicServiceImpl.saveOwner`** (sequence sourcing) — the sequence is now *per-city* ("one more than the owners already in that city") instead of global. I added a small private `countOwnersInCity(city)` helper that counts existing owners in the same city case-insensitively, mirroring the existing inline `findAll()`-based approach.

**`OwnerMapper.formatMembershipNumber`** — this already builds the membership number from `owner.getCustomerCode()` (`"<customerCode>-M<YY>"`), so it automatically rebuilds on the new format with no code change. I only updated the stale javadoc example (`SMI-0007-M26` → `LON-SMI-0007-M26`) to match.

The new acceptance test `coreCustomerCodeHasCityPrefix` (asserting the `[A-Z]{3}-[A-Z]{3}-\d{4}` shape) and the full suite pass.
